    The restacked Gym merge sequence

    The corrected draft is an eight-PR dependency chain. Review and merge it in order because each PR targets the branch immediately before it. The complete production-participant recovery test is part of the top PR, #2946.

    Existing Gym pull requests

    1. #2939 — propagate stable execution identity
    2. #2940 — add fenced control contracts
    3. #2941 — add the policy model participant
    4. #2942 — current whitebox agent participant; re-cut into episode-processor and agent-session participants
    5. #2943 — current SimpleAgent continuation; move protocol position into the single-agent episode processor
    6. #2944 — current Gymnasium continuation; split episode-step orchestration from private agent session state
    7. #2945 — add the resources state participant
    8. #2946 — adapt initial stateful environments and add the end-to-end checkpoint cycle

    Integration work after the Gym stack

    The following milestones describe remaining cross-repository work. They are not additional claims about what PRs #2939–#2946 already implement.

    Two NeMo-RL draft pull-request layers

    1. RL #4092 — identity layer: propagates stable _ng_rollout_id and numeric _ng_attempt_index through dispatch, result handling, token staging, and recovery. Attempt zero uses the logical capture key; later attempts use -aN.
    2. RL #4093 — NemoGym participant layer: adds the live-execution registry, exact result acknowledgement, participant discovery, deadline-bounded lifecycle methods, manifest integrity, the Gym #2946 pin, and cross-repository tests. It depends on #4092 and excludes SingleController. It currently discovers model, agent, and resources participants and must be revised to include episode processors plus private agent-session participants.

    Both layers implement work under #3225 — Training-framework integrations for partial rollout checkpointing. The second layer addresses #3229 — Integrate the NeMo-RL NemoGym actor with Gym checkpoint participants.

    Remaining milestone 1 — Add Gym to the existing controller transaction

    1. Land NeMo-RL #4092 and its dependent actor participant in #4093, then wire that actor into SingleController.
    2. Prepare Gym before the existing data-plane checkpoint barrier so every selected completed call or cut prefix reaches durable custody. Commit Gym manifests into the same temporary checkpoint bundle while the existing TQ, replay, recovery-ledger, and dataloader state are frozen.
    3. Make inline and staged prefix delivery explicit and mutually exclusive. Preserve one integrity contract while allowing vLLM to fetch a staging chain under #3227 and Megatron Inference to receive inline tokens under #3228.
    4. For Megatron checkpoint support, build the active-prefix cut on top of the unified completed-call staging in NeMo-RL #3869.
    5. On restore, load the existing native data-plane checkpoint before Gym participants, then reconcile every restored model coordinate against the restored inventory.
    6. Extend the existing atomic controller publication so its global marker names and authenticates every required Gym manifest.

    Exit condition: completed captured rollouts and groups survive a controller restart with the same exact token rows. An unfinished rollout restarts from input without selecting staged rows from its abandoned attempt.

    Remaining milestone 2 — Controller-selected episode continuation

    1. Adopt EpisodeId as the stable rollout and attempt contract shared by rollout collection, checkpoint control, agent sessions, resources sessions, and model lineage.
    2. Move active /run tracking, parking, result acknowledgement, and protocol-boundary persistence from the agent participant into an episode-processor participant.
    3. Split private agent state into AgentSessionSnapshot. Stateless agents need no payload; stateful agents export only data that cannot be reconstructed from processor-owned requests and responses.
    4. Do not publish while processor status reports parked-without-boundary or completed-unacknowledged episodes, or while a referenced component session cannot produce a compatible snapshot.
    5. Restore model lineage, resources sessions, agent sessions, and runtimes before restoring episode processor boundaries.
    6. Reconcile each boundary's last model-call ID, resources revision, and agent activation with the model manifest, resources manifests, agent-session manifests, and restored TransferQueue rows before releasing the processor.

    Exit condition: a supported episode processor resumes between protocol operations without repeating a completed seed, activation, verification, or close. Any private agent session it references restores first.

    Remaining milestone 3 — Stateful resources reconciliation

    1. Start restore-expected resources servers as fresh paused processes and pass their namespaced manifests to the implemented restore routes.
    2. Verify each processor boundary's recorded resources revision and resources-session identity before dispatch, and define the shared acknowledgement that permits completed-session tombstone cleanup.
    3. Require nested judge and simulator calls to use auxiliary model instances that remain available during policy-model prepare.
    4. Apply the deadline policy only to sessions whose implementation declares that its partial state and external effects can be discarded safely.

    Exit condition: an episode processor and its logical environment session restore under a replacement attempt. Resources state and any private agent session install before the processor resumes.

    Milestone 4 — Blackbox runtime continuation

    1. Add a checkpoint-aware egress relay inside the runtime boundary.
    2. Add one runtime provider that can freeze and restore the complete harness process tree and memory.
    3. Capture pending requests and cached responses, then remap endpoints and attempt identity before resume.
    4. Keep providers without full-runtime support explicitly restart_only.

    Exit condition: an opaque harness resumes from a full runtime snapshot without losing, duplicating, or misattributing a model or resources request.

    Existing evidence and the new integration gap

    The checkpoint stack tests model, agent-owned boundary, resources, stale-attempt, manifest, and restore mechanics. The episode orchestration stack beginning at #3482 separately tests processor admission, typed episode identity, resources and agent session setup, /v1/responses activation, verification, cleanup, routing, and one real Hermes plus SWE Pro rollout. Neither stack tests a checkpoint where the episode processor owns the boundary and the agent server owns only private session state. That joined crash-and-restore test is now required before claiming episode continuation.

    Known limitations of the current draft

    • The existing Gym checkpoint stack puts active /run ownership and protocol boundaries in agent servers. It must be re-cut around the episode processor architecture in the public Gym stack beginning at #3482.
    • EpisodeContext cleanup callbacks are process-local and always unwind from BaseEpisodeProcessor.run. The episode stack does not yet persist protocol position, participant handles, or cleanup obligations.
    • The NemoGym actor in NeMo-RL #4093 discovers model, agent, and resources participants. It must include episode processors and private agent-session participants, and SingleController still does not invoke it or publish a global checkpoint.
    • The Gym and actor end-to-end tests simulate token staging coordinates. NeMo-RL separately exercises real native TransferQueue save and restore, but no current test joins that path to these Gym manifests or a real vLLM or Megatron active-generation cut.
    • Multi-worker admission and exact receipt aggregation have a protocol and test harness, but production launcher and control-URL wiring are absent.
    • Commit, restore, and resume carry deadlines but do not bound every filesystem or adapter callback with them.
    • The artifact format writes individual rollout files. A bounded archive format is still needed before adopting it for large live sets.
    • Opaque blackbox harnesses still need a full runtime snapshot and egress relay. Descriptor reconnect alone cannot preserve process memory or pending calls.
    Partial-rollout checkpointing · proposed NeMo-RL and NeMo Gym architecture · aligned with public Gym PR stack #3482–#3492 · self-contained HTML, inline CSS/JS/SVG

    Part 4

    From v1 to v2

    The v1 design planned an episode processor that owns the rollout lifecycle, and it described a Gym implementation in the eight-PR chain #2939–#2946. The episode processor landed on main as the environment server. v2 re-cuts the checkpoint stack around it and removes much of the machinery v1 needed, because a single owner of the episode protocol, plus a fixed participant order, makes a consistent cut without after-the-fact reconciliation.

    At a glance

    Topicv1v2
    Who records where an episode continuesThe agent's /run in the implementation; an episode processor in the planThe environment server records a boundary after each step. Agents and resources servers export only their own session state
    A step in flight at a checkpointDrain it, or retire the rolloutEach step is wait (the default) or replay, declared by whoever implements it
    Participant orderThe training framework's actor sequences model, agent, and resources participantsGym owns the order. The framework calls Gym's checkpoint coordination
    Finished rollouts during a checkpointResults are cached until a receipt-bound acknowledgementNo episode completes while Gym is prepared. No acknowledgements
    In-flight generationsAccepted generations finish staging before prepare completesPrepare never waits for a generation. Undelivered responses are held and left out; a generation cut can keep the prefix
    Model-call lineage across a restoreA one-shot restored-parent header relayLedger rows are restored under the replacement attempt, so the parent resolves normally
    Resources consistencyPer-session mutation locks, revisions, request-ID receipts, and controller-side reconciliationThe order does it: agents park before resources close, and resources drain in-flight requests
    Control APIPer-kind routes, capability discovery, instance rolesOne route set per server and a status probe; a model participates only with an explicit policy opt-in
    StorageOne file per rollout, with archive shards plannedOne records file and one manifest per participant
    Servers without checkpoint supportDeclared through capabilities; undeclared servers could be missedEvery environment server, agent, resources server and the policy model server participates. A rollout that some server cannot capture is a restart: reported in prepare, never blocking, and started over after a crash
    Multi-worker serversA worker-coordinator protocol, not yet wired into startupPolicy model servers run several uvicorn workers as one participant: a coordinator in the main process and, in each worker, an admission gate and a worker link, over a Unix socket. Every other server kind does the same, with session routing: a session's requests reach the worker that holds it, and the worker count may change between a checkpoint and a restore
    Calls during a checkpointRefused with 409, and callers retriedWait for resume without being admitted, so a harness never sees a refusal and prepare never counts the call
    Evaluation runsNot coveredRollout collection is the controller: it checkpoints on a signal or a timer, and a dispatch log lets a resumed run retire what the crashed run sent and send it again as a later attempt
    Controller lossThe actor's mutex and deadlinesAlso a lease: each participant resumes on its own if the controller stops calling

    Scalability and ergonomics

    v1 was correct in intent but expensive to run and to build on. Most of its cost came from components reconciling each other after the fact. v2 removes that need, so the cost of a checkpoint stays small as rollouts grow in number and length:

    Cost in v1How v2 avoids it
    One acknowledgement per completed rollout, sent during checkpoints; bursts of these competed with the checkpoint itself at high concurrencyNo acknowledgements: nothing completes while Gym is prepared, and results already sent are simply waited for
    Client-side polling of each participant kind until readyOne server-side wait per participant, with a bounded list of blockers
    Per-mutation revisions and request receipts on every tool call, paid on the normal pathNothing on the normal path: the participant order gives a consistent cut
    The controller joined continuation indexes with storage references to know which token-store rows to keepThe model's commit reply lists the token-store keys the checkpoint keeps
    The controller sequenced every participant and parsed a different reply shape for each kindGym's coordination functions own the order; every participant has the same routes and replies
    One file per rolloutOne records file per participant; restore writes are batched and kept off the request path
    Servers that declared nothing could be missedEvery server takes part; undeclared servers are restart-only, and their rollouts never hold up a checkpoint
    Multi-worker model servers needed a coordinator that was never wired into startupEvery server kind runs several workers as one participant: a coordinator in its main process and a worker link in each worker, with sessions routed to the worker that holds them
    Control calls shared connections with long-running rollout callsControl calls use their own connection pool

    A process-level test suite checkpoints real Gym servers mid-episode, kills them, restores, and checks the exact model calls that follow. It covers native and legacy episodes, stateful environments, token lineage, generation cuts, a second crash before a replacement starts, servers with several workers, a deployment that mixes saved and restarted rollouts, rollout collection preempted and resumed, and a scale scenario with thousands of concurrent rollouts.

    v1 mechanisms that v2 removes

    v1 mechanismWhy v1 needed itWhat replaces it in v2
    Receipt-bound completed-result acknowledgementA finished result could be lost between Gym and the framework during a checkpointNothing completes while Gym is prepared. Before its barrier, the framework waits for its outstanding /run replies whose episodes no participant exported. A lost reply is an ordinary failure, retried as the next attempt
    Agent prepare polling and the model status long pollReadiness was a client-side loop over per-kind callsOne prepare call per participant waits server-side until ready or the deadline, then returns its blockers
    One-shot restored-parent relay headersThe first resumed call had to find its parent from the old attemptThe restored ledger belongs to the replacement attempt, so parent resolution is unchanged
    Resources mutation locks, revisions, and request-ID receiptsAn exported resources snapshot had to agree with the agent's boundaryThe order guarantees it. A tool call runs between agent boundaries, so it blocks agent prepare, and resources prepare last
    Controller-side boundary reconciliation (last model-call ID, resources revision)Files written at different moments could describe different cutsParticipants are frozen in dependency order and commit re-checks readiness. Restore is scoped to the episodes the framework continues and is all or nothing
    Capability discovery, instance roles, the plane header, spinup validationThe actor had to classify servers and pick participantsGET …/checkpoint/status: a server without the routes is not a participant; a model joins only with an explicit policy opt-in
    Worker-membership proofs and the response-egress fence for generation cutsCuts had to be aggregated across uvicorn workersOne process holds the undelivered responses and records its cuts. A failed cut regenerates the call
    A restore_failed_paused phaseA failed restore had to stay observable and pausedCoordination retires the replacement attempts everywhere and resumes; those rollouts restart from input as later attempts
    The actor's participant order tablesThe framework sequenced the participants itselfGym's checkpoint coordination owns prepare, commit, restore, resume, and retire

    What stays the same

    • Identity: _ng_rollout_id and _ng_attempt_index, and the capture key r or r-aN. v1 refused a replaced attempt's requests forever; v2 refuses the requests of a retired attempt, or of one a restore replaced, until the controller forgets its rollout.
    • Every control call carries a checkpoint ID and an absolute deadline; repeating a completed call returns the recorded result; a stale checkpoint ID cannot reopen traffic.
    • Manifests are written last, and a committed participant directory never changes.
    • Restore installs attempt N's state as attempt N+1, in fresh processes, and stays closed until an explicit resume.
    • Durable token storage and global publication stay with the training framework. Gym stores token-free coordinates.
    • Failure handling is fail-closed.

    Names

    One name per concept, the same in code, status reports, PR descriptions and this page. Earlier names, from v1 or from earlier drafts of v2, map as follows:

    ConceptEarlier nameName now
    Removing an attempt from Gymretire and fence: a per-rollout minimum attempt kept forever retire: mark, stop, then free; forget ends the mark. RetiredAttempts refuses a rollout's retired attempts, and the attempts a restore replaced, until forget, and the status report counts them as retired_rollouts, which also counts rollouts kept only for the marks a restore left
    Refusing work while admission is closedcheckpoint_parked (policy model, agents, environment servers), resources_admission_closed (resources servers) checkpoint_admission_closed on every server
    The per-server object that runs the phase machinecontroller, ParticipantController control plane, ParticipantControlPlane. "Controller" means only whoever calls coordination: NeMo RL, or rollout collection
    Checkpoint IDs a resume has closedretired checkpoint IDsresumed checkpoint IDs, of which the last 64 are remembered
    Restored state no replacement attempt has claimedpending, unused, not yet re-dispatched unclaimed; unclaimed() and the status key unclaimed in code
    What a commit does with unclaimed restored state its scope leaves outrelease, drop delete; delete_restored in code, which defaults to retire where a retire refuses nothing later
    What a participant does with an attempt's state once its work stoppedrelease, discard free
    The commit scopethe model commit scope: episodes the other participants exported commit scope: every episode the controller continues, for every participant
    The marker that refuses a retired capture's late writestombstone (complete-record store), fence (capture ledger)fence in both; delete removes the data and the fence
    The attempt in generation-cut wire modelsattempt_indexattempt, as in EpisodeId
    The cut prefix a re-issued call continuesgeneration_token_count, digest prefix_token_count, prefix_digest, as in the worker's acknowledgement
    Worker identityworker ID, for two different valuesowner: the worker a session belongs to; routing ID: a worker's own ID in cookies and MCP session tokens; worker index: the coordinator's number for a registered worker
    Per-worker checkpoint piecesgate, linkworker link for control; admission gate only for the policy model's admission
    Session routing tables after a restorea table, a second table; then the alias table and the placement tablerouting claims: one file per session ID, in a directory the workers share, naming the worker that holds the session; a restore rewrites the claims of the sessions it installs
    The token a cookieless harness sends with tool callssigned token, tool-call token, MCP tokenMCP session token
    What a server's code can savecheckpoint_sessions_supported (agents), checkpoint_boundaries (environment servers), ResourcesCheckpointModecheckpoint mode: checkpoint_mode, one of restart_only, stateless and exported, on every server kind
    Whether a checkpoint waits for a step still runningStepMode, verify_mode, verify mode, step modestep type, wait or replay; StepType. The resources server's checkpoint_verify, its status key verify and the x-ng-checkpoint-verify header keep their names
    A re-issued call with no usable cutrestartregenerated; cut_regenerate_reason. "Restart" means only a whole rollout starting over
    An agent answering a run it already finishedreplayed()saved reply; answered_from_saved_reply()
    Refusing a retired attempt's sessions as the attempt is markedfence_retiredmark; mark_retired_sessions. Participants mark; fence is only the capture ledger's and complete-record store's
    The policy model's checkpoint settingscheckpoint_policy, checkpoint_generation_cutsone checkpoint: block in the model server's instance config, {policy, generation_cuts}
    Checkpoint error codesunprefixed, such as stale_checkpoint and invalid_checkpoint_statethe checkpoint_ prefix on every one, such as checkpoint_admission_closed, checkpoint_stale and checkpoint_invalid_state

    v1 milestones in v2

    v1 milestoneStatus in v2
    1. Preserve captured tokens for stateless rolloutsImplemented by the policy model participant. Servers still need to declare themselves stateless; so far only the example servers do (see the gaps below)
    2. Resume an episode processor at a protocol boundaryImplemented on environment servers: boundaries after each step, wait or replay steps, and single_agent_turn stages. Legacy /run agents continue through the same step tracker
    3. Resume a whitebox agent with stateful resourcesImplemented for Simple Agent and exported-mode resources servers (the session-counter example). Other stateful environments need their own adapters
    4. Resume an opaque blackbox runtimeIts rollouts are restarts: they never hold up a checkpoint and start over after a crash. Saving them through sandbox snapshots needs the two pieces in the known gaps
    Generation-safe cuts (#3218, #3227)Implemented, with the same wire models as the vLLM worker proposal, the worker-side staging helpers, and a per-backend cut address. Megatron inline prefixes (#3228) are not addressed

    v1's known limitations

    v1 limitationStatus
    The stack puts protocol boundaries in agent servers and must be re-cut around the episode processorDone: the environment server owns boundaries
    Cleanup obligations are process-localBoundaries record the open session handles, so a replacement attempt reuses or closes them
    The framework actor must discover episode processors and agent sessionsReplaced by Gym's coordination, which discovers every participant
    Tests simulate token staging; no real active-generation cut is exercisedA process-level suite covers crash and restore across real server processes with a fake worker, and a real-vLLM smoke test covers turn continuation. A real active-generation cut is still untested
    Multi-worker admission is not wired into startupDone for every server kind. A worker that has not reported, or was lost during a checkpoint, blocks it; a worker that joins mid-checkpoint closes at once
    Commit, restore, and resume do not bound every filesystem callParticipant file I/O runs off the event loop under the request deadline
    The artifact format writes one file per rolloutOne records file per participant
    Opaque harnesses need a full runtime snapshotStill true for saving them; meanwhile their rollouts are restarts and never block a checkpoint

    Review feedback on the v1 implementation

    The 23 open review threads on #2939–#2946 fall into these groups:

    • Races between control operations (resume during prepare, delayed messages, wakeups crossing checkpoints): one lock serializes every transition, prepare re-checks its checkpoint after waiting, and resumed checkpoint IDs are remembered and refused.
    • Parent and identity propagation (agent middleware, the parent relay, headers versus URL prefixes): only the URL prefix remains, and the parent relay is gone.
    • Unfinished model calls saved too early: undelivered calls and their ledger rows are always left out.
    • Restore with live state, and stale attempts: every participant refuses restore with live state. Retire stops an attempt's work and frees its state before it replies, and the refusal of the attempt lasts until the controller forgets the rollout.
    • Restored state that no replacement has claimed yet, lost by a second checkpoint: this concern also applied to v2 and is fixed: every participant exports unclaimed restored state again while the controller's scope continues it.
    • Terminal sessions not reported to the checkpoint layer: resources servers get explicit session-start and session-end hooks for protocols that create sessions outside /seed_session.

    Work built on v1

    WorkIn v2
    Gym #3349, turn-level recoveryReceipts, acknowledgements, parent relay, revisions, and archive formats are superseded. Its stateless and replay declarations for math, code, judge, and GenRM servers, and its re-checkpoint-before-restart test, carry forward
    Gym #3412, prefix recoveryThe widened cut contract carried over. Worker staging helpers and restarting constrained-decoding requests carry forward
    Gym #3563, multi-worker policy serverSupported with the same shape (a main-process coordinator, a Unix socket, restored cuts with a single owner), without proof or evidence files: workers report in memory and the coordinator holds the one control plane
    Gym #3755, scale optimizationsAcknowledgement batching is moot; concurrent commits and blocker caps are built in. A reserved connection pool for control traffic carries forward
    Gym #3756, union of sharded cutsNot needed while each episode stays on its shard: each shard commits and restores its own episodes
    Gym #3548 and #3634, environment adaptersPort directly onto the new resources and agent hooks
    NeMo RL #4264–#4266 and #4319–#4323The framework calls Gym coordination instead of per-kind routes, drops acknowledgements and continuation joins, and adds the wait for outstanding /run replies. The cut wire models are unchanged; the enable flag and import path moved

    Gaps

    What is still open is listed with the v2 design, under known gaps. These gaps, found while building v2, are closed:

    • Unclaimed restored state survives a second checkpoint, and a commit deletes restored state its scope no longer continues.
    • The worker-side staging helpers for generation cuts are in Gym, and backends that serve cuts at another address name one per backend; a backend without one fails its cut, which only costs regenerating the call.
    • Twenty training verifiers declare themselves stateless with replayable verification. Every other server still takes part as restart-only.
    • A replay-mode verification is admitted during a checkpoint, and a seed waits for resume.
    • Control calls use their own connection pool.
    • Agents, resources servers and environment servers run several workers, and the worker count may change between a checkpoint and a restore.
    • Calls with constrained decoding are never cut. The commit reply lists the token-store keys a checkpoint keeps, per episode.
    • Retire stops, then frees; the refusal of a retired attempt lasts until the controller forgets the rollout, and only the most recent checkpoint IDs are kept.
    • A rollout that some server cannot capture no longer holds up every checkpoint: it is a restart.
    • A restore refuses the attempts it replaces until the controller forgets them, and a failed export ends its checkpoint instead of being exported again.
    • A new policy call during a checkpoint waits instead of being refused.
    • Gym never sends a /run again after a dropped connection, which used to orphan agent sessions.
    • A resumed evaluation run retires what the crashed run sent after its checkpoint and sends it again as a later attempt, and it repeats a retire that failed.
    • Each server keeps its sockets in one runtime directory that it removes at exit, and a new server removes those that killed servers left behind.
